leading_positions.synthesis: Three members prefer topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect as a single-part prize. Johansson and Olsson name Kane, Mele and Molenkamp from the start; Danielsson moved to the same trio in his round-1 response after proposing Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan in the opening. They share the case of a prediction-plus-first-realisation chain with fifteen to twenty years of independent confirmation. The citations are worded differently: Danielsson's refers to Z2 topological insulators and the HgTe quantum wells, Johansson's and Olsson's to the quantum spin Hall state, Z2 classification and first HgTe observation. Danielsson and Johansson would accept Hasan only if the citation were to cover the 3D branch, at the cost of a theory slot. Not shared: how much weight the 2016 topological-phases prize carries, and whether the omitted Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu, Moore and Balents contributions should affect the case. Olsson explicitly names B034 as the cleaner configuration if credit is judged to misstate the original work.

Three members include the optical lattice clock with Katori and Ye in their preferred configuration; Kroll and Lindroth propose it as a single-part prize and I propose it as one part of a two-part prize with B005. Shared: the two-name credit maps onto proposal (magic-wavelength lattice) and realisation (record accuracy and stability), and the 10^-18 results have been independently reproduced. Differences: Kroll cites the pending redefinition of the second as supporting context, Lindroth treats it as supporting but not necessary, and Danielsson and Mehlig explicitly disagree that it adds to the merit. Citation wording differs on invention versus development versus realisation. Not shared: Kroll, Lindroth and I accept that other lattice-clock groups may have priority claims, but we differ on how far that should limit a two-name prize. Kroll has disclosed a possible proximity to the Hall laboratory environment.

Two members prefer magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene as a single-part prize. Both credit MacDonald for the continuum-model prediction and Jarillo-Herrero for the 2018 correlated-insulator and superconductivity experiments, and both see a rare prediction-then-experiment chain. They differ on the third laureate: Eriksson names Bistritzer, whose co-authorship of the 2011 continuum model he regards as essential, while Mehlig names Andrei for earlier STM and transport evidence of flat bands. Their citations also differ: Eriksson's names the prediction of flat bands at the magic angle plus the experimental discovery in twisted bilayer graphene, while Mehlig's broadens the experimental part to moire flat-band systems. Both acknowledge that maturity (about eight years, unsettled pairing mechanism) is the weakest dimension, and Eriksson says he could be persuaded to recognise B028 first.

One member (the chair, speaking as a member) proposes a two-part prize combining the optical lattice clock (Katori, Ye) with IceCube astrophysical neutrinos (Halzen alone). No other member includes B005 in a preferred configuration; Danielsson ranked it second in the opening and in his response judged a single-name prize for a large collaboration too fragile for this round. Kroll questioned who made the first statistically decisive observation. The proposer himself identifies the one-name credit as the weakest element and says the astroparticle part falls away if it cannot be justified, leaving the clock alone.

areas_of_agreement: No configuration has a majority: B028 has three explicit supporters, B034 has three, B046 has two, and B005 has one. All eight members place B028, B034 and B046 among the three or four serious candidates, either as preferred configuration or as listed alternatives.

Every member who commented on the topological-insulator trio agrees that Kane and Mele should not be separated, since the Z2 invariant and the quantum spin Hall proposal are a joint result. Danielsson accepted this in his round-1 response.
Members agree that B034 has the cleanest attribution on the shortlist, a two-name credit that maps onto proposal and realisation, even where they disagree that clean credit settles scientific merit.

Members agree that the superconducting pairing mechanism in twisted bilayer graphene is unsettled and that the prize claim would have to rest on the flat bands and correlated phases, not on the mechanism.
Members agree that the credited-name lists for B028 and B046 do not cover every claimant, and that any three-name set leaves out someone with a defensible claim.
scientific_disputes: B028 versus B034: Johansson and Olsson regard topological classification as a new class of quantum matter that reorganised condensed matter, photonics and materials search, and Johansson describes B034 as an advance in precision of an established technique. Kroll and Lindroth regard the clock as an invention-type discovery with settled interpretation and uses in tests of fundamental constants and geodesy. Eriksson adds that B034 is more an instrument achievement than a new regime of matter and that the fundamental-physics results it should enable have not yet arrived.

Whether the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 prize for quantum control of single ions weaken novelty for B034: Mehlig and Kroll raise it, while Lindroth argues the magic-wavelength lattice clock is a distinct scheme and that Ye's credited contribution is the strontium clock realisation, not the comb.

Whether the 2016 prize on topological phases and phase transitions overlaps B028: Lindroth treats the overlap as more significant than Danielsson does; Danielsson, Johansson and Eriksson regard it as different (phase transitions and quantum Hall precursors versus Z2 classification and protected edge and surface states).

Whether the 2D theory-plus-HgTe story or the 3D ARPES branch is the core of the topological-insulator discovery, which Danielsson originally argued for Hasan and Johansson and Olsson answered by preferring the compact prediction-plus-first-realisation citation.

Whether neutrino astronomy is established well enough: the diffuse flux is confirmed, but source identification (NGC 1068, Galactic plane) is still developing, and only Danielsson and I ranked it at all.
attribution_disputes: B028: Mele versus Hasan for the third slot (Danielsson proposed Hasan in the opening but now supports Mele; Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson all object to dropping Mele; Johansson would accept Hasan only at the cost of a theory slot). Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang's HgTe proposal and the Fu-Kane-Mele and Moore-Balents 3D theory cannot be represented among the credited names.

B046: Bistritzer (Eriksson's round-1 configuration) versus Andrei (Mehlig's round-1 configuration) for the third slot, with Eriksson saying he would hear an argument for Andrei and Mehlig saying he would not fight hard for Andrei over Bistritzer; Cao, first author of the 2018 experiments, is outside the credited names; Mehlig argues Bistritzer is already represented by the continuum-model credit given to MacDonald.
B034: Whether a two-name prize can leave out Lemonde, Ludlow, Lisdat, Bloom and other early lattice-clock groups, and how to treat ion clocks.

B005: A one-name credit (Halzen) for a detector and analysis effort of hundreds, with AMANDA and the construction and analysis leaders uncredited; Kroll asks who made the first statistically decisive observation and says a single-name prize needs an explicit rationale.

Similar-looking proposals differ in laureates and citations: B028 trio versions differ in citation scope (3D or 2D only); B046 proposals share MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero but differ on Bistritzer or Andrei; B034 versions agree on laureates but differ on invention versus development; and Pearce's part-two B005 has no counterpart in any other configuration.
maturity_disputes: B046: the key experiments are about seven to eight years old and the pairing mechanism is debated. Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson call it a candidate for a later year; Eriksson and Mehlig regard the observation and reproduction of correlated phases as sufficient, and Mehlig argues the citation can avoid the mechanism.

B034: the redefinition of the second has not happened. Kroll cites it as support, Lindroth and Mehlig take it as not decisive, and Olsson says nothing forces the clocks to be decided this year, so some members regard waiting as legitimate.

B028: roughly fifteen to twenty years of independent confirmation make it the most mature of the three, which Eriksson and Mehlig grant as their stated fallback reason, but Lindroth and Mehlig see the 2016 prize as a possible reason to wait.
B005: Halzen's single-name credit makes the otherwise mature diffuse-flux discovery fragile for this round, while the source-association results remain early.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Kroll disclosed a doctoral research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder and acknowledged possible perceived proximity to Jun Ye's environment for B034; he left the question of recusal to the chair, and Lindroth and I both said it should be declared for the committee to weigh.
Olsson disclosed a Chalmers affiliation shared with Johansson, who also ranks B028 first with the same trio; both describe it as an institutional colleague link, not a stake in the candidates.
Pearce disclosed field proximity between his gamma-ray burst instrumentation interests and B004 (not in any preferred configuration) and would not take a lead role on that candidate.
Johansson disclosed Chalmers and WACQT ties to superconducting-circuit work; he stated they would matter only if B035 were discussed, which is not on the shortlist.

Lindroth and Eriksson noted subject proximity (precision atomic structure for B034; electronic-structure theory and magnetism for B046 and B010) without any documented personal or institutional tie to the credited names.
questions_for_round2: Should the committee choose B028, B034 or B046 as a single-part prize, and what is each supporter's order of fallback if their first choice cannot be defended on attribution?

For B028, if Kane and Mele are kept together, is Molenkamp the best third name, or should the citation be worded to cover the 3D branch at the cost of the first HgTe experiment? How should the omitted Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu, Moore and Balents contributions be handled in a citation?
For B046, should the third laureate be Bistritzer or Andrei, and does the committee consider about eight years of reproduction plus an unresolved pairing mechanism sufficient maturity for this year?

For B034, how much weight should the 2005 and 2012 prizes carry against novelty, and can a two-name credit be defended against other lattice-clock groups? Is the pending redefinition of the second a precondition for recognition or only supporting evidence?

For B005, can a single-name credit for Halzen be justified, who made the first statistically decisive observation, and should the astroparticle part be kept only if it can be defended on those grounds?

Should a two-part prize be considered at all given the three-person limit, since any B028 or B046 trio leaves no slot for another part, and what would members need to see to prefer the B034 plus B005 pairing over a single clean prize?
Does Kroll's disclosed link to the Hall laboratory environment require recusal from the B034 discussion, or can it be handled by transparency, as Lindroth and I suggested?
summary.chair_observation: The eight round-1 files show a three-way split among topological insulators (three explicit supporters), optical lattice clocks (three, one in a two-part form) and magic-angle graphene (two), with no majority. All eight members rank B028, B034 and B046 among the serious candidates, and each of the three has a different weakest point: allocation for B028, novelty and the pending redefinition for B034, and maturity for B046. The round-1 responses already moved some positions, notably Danielsson on Mele, so the remaining differences are mainly about which weakness the committee is prepared to accept. I count only positions stated in the files.
